notYet: Not yet part of Sicily and southern Italy

stages.name: Contested
stages.desc: Both sides hold towns or armies here

stages.name: Roman home front
stages.desc: Rome and its Italian colonies and allies

stages.name: Roman Sicily
stages.desc: Main towns held by or allied to Rome

states.name: Cosenza
timeline: The Bruttians submit to Rome
The Sila forest gives Rome timber and pitch

states.name: Crotone
timeline: Croton falls into the Roman orbit
Croton, a Greek city much reduced by war

states.name: Catanzaro
timeline: The Bruttians submit to Rome
The narrow waist of Bruttium

states.name: Reggio Calabria
timeline: Rome retakes Rhegium from mutinous Campanian troops
Rhegium is the Italian shore of the crossing to Sicily
The elephants land on the Italian side of the strait

states.name: Vibo Valentia
timeline: The Bruttian coast passes to Rome
Hipponium, a former Greek city on the Tyrrhenian coast

states.name: Potenza
timeline: The Lucanians submit to Rome
Lucanian uplands, allied to Rome

states.name: Salerno
timeline: Paestum becomes a Latin colony
Paestum sends ships and crews to the fleet
A storm off this coast wrecks more than 150 ships

states.name: Naples
timeline: Neapolis becomes Rome's ally
Greek Neapolis provides ships and sailors

states.name: Caserta
timeline: Cales becomes a Latin colony
Capua and Campania, rich in grain and horsemen, serve Rome

states.name: Latina
timeline: Tarracina becomes a Roman colony
Coastal colonies guard the road to Campania

states.name: Rome
timeline: Rome dominates Latium
Rome launches a new fleet to replace the ships lost off Camarina
The captured elephants are shown in the Circus

states.name: Trapani
timeline: Lilybaeum and Drepana are Carthage's western strongholds
A Roman attack on Drepana fails; inland, Segesta has sided with Rome since the 260s
Hasdrubal's army and elephants are based at Lilybaeum about this time
Carthage empties Selinus; Rome begins the long siege of Lilybaeum

states.name: Messina
timeline: Messana admits a Roman garrison, the act that began the war
Tyndaris goes over to Rome; Lipara stays Carthaginian
The consul Aurelius Cotta takes Lipara
The captured elephants are ferried across the strait

states.name: Palermo
timeline: Panormus is Carthage's great base on the north coast
Rome storms Panormus, but Thermae and the height of Herkte stay with Carthage
A Roman attempt to seize Thermae by treachery fails
Thermae falls; Rome holds the coast, though Herkte still resists
Metellus keeps his army inside Panormus, wary of the elephants on the plain
Metellus destroys Hasdrubal's attack and captures the elephants

states.name: Agrigento
timeline: Rome takes Agrigentum after a long siege and sells its people
Carthalo burns Agrigentum and tears down its walls

states.name: Caltanissetta
timeline: Rome takes Mytistratum after hard sieges
Hill towns of the interior, watched by Roman garrisons

states.name: Ragusa
timeline: The south-eastern corner lies in or beside Hiero's kingdom
The coast of Camarina, where Rome's fleet was wrecked in 255 BC

states.name: Syracuse
timeline: Hiero of Syracuse makes peace with Rome and keeps his kingdom
Syracuse, rich and fortified, supplies its Roman ally
Hiero lends ships for the attack on Lipara, according to Zonaras

states.name: Catania
timeline: Catana comes over to Rome; Leontini to the south is Hiero's
Catana and the towns below Etna remain Roman allies

states.name: Enna
timeline: Rome retakes Enna from Carthage
Enna, at the island's centre, stays in Roman hands

states.name: Benevento
timeline: Beneventum becomes a Latin colony
Beneventum, near where Rome fought Pyrrhus and his elephants in 275 BC

states.name: Frosinone
timeline: Fregellae is founded as a Latin colony
The Latin colonies of the Liris valley supply troops

states.name: Avellino
timeline: The Samnite uplands are under Rome's control
Hirpini uplands owe soldiers to Rome

events.title: A new fleet
events.text: After the wreck off Camarina, Rome builds 220 ships in three months, according to Polybius.

events.title: Survivors join at Messana
events.text: The new fleet picks up the ships that survived the storm, making about 300 sail.

events.title: Agrigentum burned
events.text: The Carthaginian Carthalo takes and burns Agrigentum, then tears down its walls.

events.title: Cephaloedium betrayed
events.text: The consuls win the town of Cephaloedium by treachery.

events.title: Drepana holds out
events.text: A Roman attack on the harbour town of Drepana fails.

events.title: Panormus besieged
events.text: The consuls throw up works in two places and bring up battering rams.

events.title: New Town stormed
events.text: A tower on the shore collapses, and Roman soldiers break into the New Town.

events.title: Old Town yields
events.text: The people of the Old Town, cut off, surrender on terms.

events.title: Thirteen thousand enslaved
events.text: Diodorus says 14,000 people bought their freedom for two minas each, and 13,000 were sold.

events.title: Ietas expels its garrison
events.text: The hill town of Ietas drives out its Carthaginian garrison and joins Rome.

events.title: Solus joins Rome
events.text: Solus, east of Panormus, follows Ietas to the Roman side.

events.title: Tyndaris joins Rome
events.text: Tyndaris, on the north coast, also leaves Carthage.

events.title: Roman garrison at Panormus
events.text: Panormus, with a Roman garrison, is now the main Roman port in western Sicily.

events.title: Failure before Lilybaeum
events.text: The consuls Servilius and Sempronius attempt Lilybaeum without success, then raid Africa.

events.title: Return from Africa
events.text: After running aground on the shoals of Meninx, the Roman fleet limps back to Panormus.

events.title: Storm wrecks the fleet
events.text: On the open-sea passage home, a storm destroys more than 150 Roman ships.

events.title: Trap at Thermae
events.text: A gatekeeper lets in a thousand Romans, who are cut down inside the gate.

events.title: Elephants reach Lilybaeum
events.text: Carthage sends Hasdrubal to Sicily with about 140 elephants; the date is uncertain.

events.title: Thermae falls
events.text: Rome takes Thermae; Zonaras says Carthage had carried off its people.

events.title: Hiero lends ships
events.text: Hiero of Syracuse provides ships for the attack on Lipara, according to Zonaras.

events.title: Lipara falls
events.text: The consul Aurelius Cotta takes the island of Lipara; Zonaras says he killed its inhabitants.

events.title: Herkte defies Rome
events.text: A Roman army tries and fails to take the height of Herkte, near Panormus.

events.title: Cotta punishes his cavalry
events.text: The consul Aurelius Cotta deals harshly with cavalrymen who refuse his orders.

events.title: Legions avoid the plains
events.text: For two years, Romans near Selinus and Lilybaeum refuse to meet the elephants on open ground.

events.title: Metellus becomes consul
events.text: Lucius Caecilius Metellus and Gaius Furius take up the consulship.

events.title: Sixty supply ships
events.text: Rome mans only sixty ships, enough to feed its army in Sicily.

events.title: Hiero feeds his allies
events.text: Hiero's kingdom remains Rome's ally and a source of supplies.

events.title: Elephants dominate the west
events.text: Hasdrubal's army holds the open country around Lilybaeum.

events.title: Furius sails home
events.text: One consul returns to Italy with half of the army.

events.title: Metellus holds Panormus
events.text: Metellus stays with the rest to protect the allies' harvest.

events.title: Hasdrubal marches
events.text: Hasdrubal leads his army from Lilybaeum through hard passes toward Panormus.

events.title: Spies unmasked
events.text: Metellus finds Carthaginian spies by having the townspeople seize strangers, says Zonaras.

events.title: Harvest destroyed
events.text: Hasdrubal ravages the crops up to the city's edge while Metellus keeps still.

events.title: Across the river
events.text: The Carthaginian army and its elephants cross the river before Panormus.

events.title: Javelins from the ditch
events.text: Light troops in a ditch shower the elephants with missiles, and the beasts turn on their own men.

events.title: Metellus attacks
events.text: Heavy infantry charge from a gate into the disordered Carthaginian flank.

events.title: Elephants captured
events.text: Ten are taken with their drivers, the rest afterwards; totals range from 60 to 142.

events.title: Rafts cross the strait
events.text: The elephants are ferried to Italy on decks laid over rows of jars.

events.title: Triumph and Circus
events.text: Metellus celebrates a triumph and the elephants are shown in the Circus; Pliny's sources disagree about whether they were killed.

events.title: Hasdrubal condemned
events.text: Hasdrubal escapes to Lilybaeum; Carthage later recalls and executes him.

events.title: Selinus razed
events.text: Carthage destroys Selinus and moves its people to Lilybaeum.

events.title: Siege of Lilybaeum
events.text: The consuls Atilius and Manlius begin a siege that will last almost a decade.

chartNote: Share of the mapped land area, by the power holding the main towns of each present-day province, with Italy's Roman home front included. Control in the First Punic War was held town by town, and several boundaries here are judgements: the coast around Panormus is marked contested until Thermae fell, and Hiero's inland border is uncertain. Ancient dates are approximate; some historians put the battle of Panormus in 251 rather than 250 BC.
